extracted.intended_audience: government contracting officers, auditors, and policy analysts studying A-76 commercial activity contracts (Coast Guard/MLCPAC)
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of cost drivers, performance, administration, and modifications for Coast Guard commercial activity contracts (food service, security, housing maintenance) under OMB Circular A-76 in the Pacific Area. Identifies causes of cost changes and factors affecting contract success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage increases as primary cost driver
rubrics_metrics.description: Wage increases are the driving factor for increased costs in this contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations incorporated into option years and contract extensions can substantially raise contract costs (examples: nearly doubled cost in one extension; multiple option-year wage adjustments listed). Track DOL determinations and whether increases were taken in each option year; equitable adjustments may compensate for previously untaken increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deobligation when actual costs are below estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: A deobligation occurs when the actual costs of performance in a contract are below the original estimated cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When actual activity (e.g., meals sold) falls below estimates, excess obligated funds are transferred elsewhere. Example: reductions in meals sold resulted in deobligations that offset wage or price increases; COTR confirmation via monthly invoices used to verify. Ensure deobligations are recorded in contract files to explain year-to-year differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meal pricing tied to volume ranges (food service contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: In food service contracts, each type of meal is priced based on a range of the number of meals sold each month, with a higher price per meal for a low number and a lower price per meal for a high number of meals sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sales increase and move to a higher range, meal prices reduce; if sales decrease into the lowest range, per-meal price is highest but total entitlement may be less than originally obligated, triggering deobligation. Monitor meal-volume ranges and adjust estimates accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measured by deductions for unsatisfactory performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract performance is assessed and may result in deductions for unsatisfactory performance; many contracts reported 'no deductions taken' indicating satisfactory performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of deductions (amounts and reasons). Even small deductions (e.g., $446 for 14 'minor discrepancies') should be recorded in contract files and reflected in payment records to validate enforcement of quality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Manager experience and continuity as success factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor’s Project Manager (PM) experience (e.g., prior Coast Guard SS background) is a major reason for contract success and for making transitions between contractors 'virtually invisible.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain PMs with relevant prior-service experience when possible; continuity of key personnel (PM retained across contract transitions) helps maintain high-quality service and user satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification clarity to prevent scope creep
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguous specifications were perceived to allow contractors to negotiate higher prices for additional work that should have been within the original scope (example: 'exercise meals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clear, well-defined Performance Work Statements (PWS) to reduce disputes and unplanned modifications; explicitly address foreseeable exceptional events (e.g., large exercises) to avoid unrecorded or out-of-scope negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration documentation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts administered under some districts 'contained little documentation' and seemed based on verbal/handshake agreements, requiring later 'patch-up' by contract specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain comprehensive contract files documenting obligations, deobligations, modifications, and decisions to allow reconstruction of contract history and justification for changes in cost or scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost reduction only achievable via requirements reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The only way to cut costs in this contract is to reduce the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When wage and price drivers dominate costs (e.g., housing maintenance), consider whether lowering service requirements is feasible; recognize this may be unlikely if service need increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for contracts studied
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for selection of the three contracts were: Pacific Area contracts to observe the same contract administration; similarity to the complexity of prior contracts; contracts that had deleted billets of the rate most severely affected by A-76 (Subsistence Specialists); commercial activities in high cost areas; and mature (completed) and current (ongoing) contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent selection criteria when sampling contracts for comparative studies to control for administrative and complexity variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications frequently driven by continuing resolutions and funding availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple contract modifications were required as a result of Congressional continuing resolutions and limited government funds available during certain periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and plan for frequent mods tied to government funding cycles; document the funding-driven mods and their effect on contract totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic price adjustments and indexes incorporated
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic price adjustments (e.g., Consumer Foods Price Index adjustments) and negotiated price modifications increased contract costs (e.g., Mod 13 Consumer Foods Price Increases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit clauses for economic price adjustments and track CPI or other indices affecting consumables; document application and effect on contract totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of contractor financial stability on operational risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor bankruptcy (Chapter 11) or financial difficulties can affect contract operations (e.g., payments diverted to IRS, restricted commissary purchases) and create operational risk if a contractor defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contractor financial stability during award and have contingency plans (e.g., availability of Government employees to perform in default scenarios, especially in remote locations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of small business programs and competition on price
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of SBA 8(a) set-aside and subsequent graduation to open small business competition affected contract pricing; small business competition drove down contract cost in one instance by $47,065/year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider procurement pathway (8(a) vs. open competition) and how contractor program status changes over time will affect future pricing and competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future requirements in new contracts should anticipate cost drivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential future requirements (e.g., guards carrying firearms) were addressed in new contracts because incorporation would increase contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate foreseeable requirement changes and include them in solicitations/awards or evaluate cost impacts in advance to avoid unexpected modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional or increased work (exercise meals, added guards) as source of mods
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional work items (exercise meals, added security guard during Desert Storm) produced contract modifications and increased costs; sometimes such work was deemed 'outside the scope' and separately negotiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define how extraordinary or surge requirements will be handled (in-scope vs. out-of-scope) and document negotiations/settlements to avoid later ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for COTR training and clarity on QA paperwork
rubrics_metrics.description: COTRs reported attending QA/COTR training but noted that QA paperwork requirements remained a 'gray area' and some COTRs felt training did not fully prepare them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive, practical COTR and QA training, with clear guidance on QA paperwork and expectations; ensure COTR continuity or thorough debriefing during turnover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiation delays and DCAA audits can delay awards and cause extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay in contract award was caused primarily by the Government due to extended negotiation preparations and time for the DCAA audit of the contractor’s proposal, requiring contract extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan procurement timelines accounting for audit durations and negotiation time; include provisions for equitable adjustments and short extensions to maintain continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of obligated vs. actual costs to explain year-to-year differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancies between obligated amounts and actual contract costs (e.g., $337,200 difference over contract) could be due to unrecorded deobligations or declining activity, and MLCPAC could not always explain gaps from contract files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contract files record obligations, deobligations, and actual performance metrics (e.g., meals sold) so financial variances can be explained and audited.
